subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Rate of Rise: The Roaster's Curve
description: A micro-lesson that makes Rate of Rise: The Roaster's Curve usable.

hook.text: Professional roasters obsess over 'rate of rise' (RoR)—how quickly the bean temperature increases per minute.

buildup.text: RoR is plotted as a curve on roasting software. The ideal shape looks like a gradually declining slope.

discovery.text: A steadily declining RoR means controlled energy transfer. Spikes or crashes create flavor defects.

twist.text: The same green coffee can taste fruity or ashy, bright or flat, depending entirely on how the RoR curve was managed.

climax.text: Modern roasting is data-driven. Temperature probes, software, and airflow sensors make RoR tracking precise.

punchline.text: A curve on a screen controls thousands of flavor molecules. Data meets craft.

quiz.question: What is 'rate of rise' (RoR) in roasting?
options: How fast the roaster machine heats up
How quickly the bean temperature increases per minute
